title: Senior asks: listFiles() uses scandir() and then is_file(). What does scandir() return for an empty folder?
explain: scandir() also returns the entries . and .. . They are folders, so is_file() is false for them and the filter removes them. Without the filter, your API would list two fake files.

title: Senior asks: a client writes the id 12345678901234567890 to a JSON file. read() decodes it, write() encodes it again. What is in the file?
explain: The number is bigger than PHP_INT_MAX, so json_decode() makes a float and the last digits are lost. After a round trip you get a float in scientific notation. Fix ideas: JSON_BIGINT_AS_STRING, or send big ids as strings.

title: Senior asks: a.json exists but is empty (0 bytes). read() calls json_decode(). What does json_last_error_msg() say?
explain: An empty string is not valid JSON. json_decode() returns null and the error is Syntax error. Your decodeJson() turns this into the answer Invalid JSON. A good message would also say the file is empty.

title: Senior asks: a user saves the URL a/b with write(). What does json_encode() store without any flag?
explain: By default json_encode() escapes / as \/ . It is still valid JSON, and json_decode() gives a/b back. Use JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES if humans read the file. Check with the other JSON flags you use.

title: PHP 8. The value 0 is set, the key b is missing. What does this print?
explain: $x ??= y assigns only when $x is null or not set. The key a holds 0, which is not null, so it stays 0. The key b is missing, so it gets 7. Do not mix it up with ?: , which treats 0 as empty.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: == compares the class and all property values, so $a == $b is true. === asks if it is the same object. $a and $b are two objects, so false. $c is a second name for $a, so true.

title: What does Node print?
explain: includes() uses the SameValueZero rule, so NaN equals NaN and it finds it. indexOf() uses strict equality, and NaN === NaN is false, so it returns -1. Prefer includes() when NaN may appear.

title: You committed on main by mistake. Nothing is pushed. You want the commit on a new branch feature, and main back to origin/main. What do you run?
options: git branch feature, then git reset --hard origin/main
git reset --hard origin/main, then git branch feature
git revert HEAD, then git checkout -b feature
explain: First make the branch feature at the current commit, so the commit has a name. Then move main back with reset --hard. If you reset first, the commit is only in the reflog. Never force-push main for this.
